description: Can an ordinary fresh camp gain a real assigned worker and persistent roster? Use the declared pre-camp footing. Establish through native dialogue, assign a willing nearby ally, then save and reload the resulting camp.

steps.label: establish_r032_camp
steps.objective: Can an ordinary fresh camp gain a real assigned worker and persistent roster? Use the declared pre-camp footing. Establish through native dialogue, assign a willing nearby ally, then save and reload the resulting camp. Success boundary: The same camp and actor retain assignment after reload, with no duplicate actor, roster entry or manufactured work completion.
proof_targets: fixture-derived follower identity and no assigned camp, recorded as setup only
accepted native World, dialogue, and menu receipts for the chosen establishment route
resulting authoritative camp identity, owner, and actual lookup OMT
same follower character ID before/after native assignment, CAMP_RESIDENT mission, matching assigned_camp, and usable job priorities
independent native postcondition observation after native assignment
invariants: fixture installation and its added follower are setup only and receive zero establishment credit
do not use physical controls, OCR, coordinates, source inference, direct NPC/camp/save mutation, or synthetic receipt injection
camp selector availability or selection alone does not prove establishment
a passing assignment verdict requires a same-run authoritative resulting camp identity, its actual lookup OMT, and the same actual assigned actor
creation and assignment are distinct: do not infer assignment from camp creation, follower placement, or selector reachability
leave missions, Food, Storage, Locker, and Patrol as separate R-032 verdicts
stop the affected claim at missing native receipt, source-binding drift, stale owner, or cleanup failure while retaining independent evidence

steps.label: verify_r032_assigned_camp_continuity
steps.objective: After the native save, main-menu quit, and process replacement, use only currently advertised native semantic actions to inspect the same follower character ID.  Verify CAMP_RESIDENT and assigned_camp still match the saved camp's actual OMT, then reopen ordinary camp work and confirm the job-priority controls remain usable without reassigning or restaging the fixture.
proof_targets: native save/quit boundary and process replacement
same follower character ID after reload
persisted CAMP_RESIDENT mission and assigned_camp matching the same camp OMT
ordinary post-reload camp-work/job-priority controls usable without a new assignment
invariants: relaunch is lifecycle evidence, not assignment credit
do not restage the fixture or create/assign a replacement follower
do not mutate NPC, camp, or save state directly
missing identity, camp match, resident mission, priority usability, or native save/quit receipt leaves continuity unproved

playtest_recipe.question: Can an ordinary fresh camp gain a real assigned worker and persistent roster?

starting_state.guidance: Use the declared coherent footing for this executable route. The standard house is the default adaptation for fire, camp and human interaction questions; it is not a substitute for a specific retained state or controlled diagnostic. Preserve owner originals.

playtest_recipe.exercise: Use the declared pre-camp footing. Establish through native dialogue, assign a willing nearby ally, then save and reload the resulting camp.
controls: play look — identify the current input owner and relevant scene.
play controls — obtain current native actions and copyable movement/wait requests.
play act ACTION [--target STABLE_ID] — select an advertised action; use live IDs, not historical examples.
play wait 5m safe — example of a batched native wait, not a required interval. Choose duration and safe/stop/ignore for the actual question; ignore can allow injury or death.
For movement, use the advertised game.move_relative request through play call --request REQUEST.json, or native overmap travel for a usable route. Stop at a decision, obstruction or danger.
play collect — collect an outstanding request instead of submitting it again.
play inspect SELECTOR — retrieve the relevant field from the returned evidence handle.
playtest_recipe.batching: Batch to the next useful observation or decision, not to a prescribed command count. Read menu replies before choosing targets. Preserve pending request IDs; inspect partial progress and continue the same request when appropriate. Read-only observations do not advance game time.
playtest_recipe.success: The same camp and actor retain assignment after reload, with no duplicate actor, roster entry or manufactured work completion.
playtest_recipe.failure: A reproducible contradiction under the stated opportunity is a finding. Preserve the first divergence and distinguish product behavior from setup, transport or stale-input faults. Do not force the expected outcome.
playtest_recipe.inconclusive: Missing source, observer, reachability, elapsed time or current input ownership leaves that part unproved. Repair incidental setup in the current run where possible; do not substitute an easier endpoint.
playtest_recipe.evidence: Use play controls evidence_logs and the actual returned selectors. Record selected source/build, run and actor/site IDs, game-time endpoints and the decisive native events. Correlate emission, receipt, decision and physical action when relevant; a log label or spoken success alone is insufficient.
playtest_recipe.finish: Save useful unfinished state through the native save action. When the run is settled, close its game/helpers, verify exit and delete generated saves/logs/captures and temporary declarations. Keep owner originals and concise current findings; no archive.
playtest_recipe.reuse: Update this recipe with proven setup, controls and diagnostic queries that change future decisions. Replace obsolete advice. Keep live IDs and one-run chronology out; prior success is scoped evidence, not a current-build guarantee.
